description_full: Central Puerto S.A. engages in the electric power generation activities in Argentina. It operates in three segments: Electric Power Generation From Conventional Sources, Electric Power Generation From Renewable Sources and Forest Activity, and Management and Operations of Thermal Plants. The company's power generation assets include combined cycle, gas and steam turbine, co-generation, hydroelectric, wind turbines, and solar panels. It also engages in the natural gas transport and distribution; forestry; and mining businesses. The company was incorporated in 1992 and is based in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

financial_summary: Central Puerto S.A. is a small-cap utilities business with a $1.6B market cap on $811M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are contracting by -3.6pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 44% against a 9% cost of capital — a 35-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 48%.

The business throws off $127M in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 4.22× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 1.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.1%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 4.5% of the shares.
